reply_text:
Last page opening: the G20 transcript.I found four predictions from 2026 that meet all four tests, plus two AGI-timing remarks that belong under undated. Only one candidate comes from a transcript of Huang's whole talk (made by a third party, singjupost.com, not Nvidia). The others come from news reports. None of them matches the four self-driving car claims you already have.

**Candidates**
- **G20 Innovation Ministerial, 2 September 2026** (on stage with Howard Lutnick; third-party transcript):
  - "what do I expect in the next 5, 10 years? Things that take 10 years are going to take 1. Things that take 1 will take a month." The prediction is about AI speeding things up, though it does not say "AI" in those words.
- **CBS interview with Jo Ling Kent, about 18 September 2026** (CBS's own article; it says "on Friday", which I worked out as 18 September):
  - "2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world." This is a dated forecast that AI will not end the world by 2030. I read it only in CBS's news story. I did not open the 46-minute extended video.
- **CES question-and-answer session, Tuesday, probably 6 January 2026** (TechSpot report only):
  - Asked how long until humanoid robots match human-level ability, Huang said: "This year."

**Undated (about when AGI arrives)**
- **G20, 2 September:** "in the next couple of years, we are going to achieve essentially what people call AGI." I put this under undated because "a couple of years" is about as vague as "a few years." If you count it as a two-year span, it moves up to candidates.
- **Lex Fridman Podcast #494 (transcript posted 23 March 2026):** asked whether AGI was 5 to 20 years away, he said "I think it's now. I think we've achieved AGI." This is a claim about the present, not a forecast. Lex Fridman's own transcript page cut off after about 20 minutes, so I took the words from Fortune's report.

**Left out**
- **Business forecasts:** $3–4 trillion a year of AI infrastructure spending by 2030, $1 trillion in AI chip revenue within two years, and "100 gigawatts" built by the end of the decade.
- **"AGI has arrived" (September, after OpenAI's "GPT-6 Astra"):** I saw this only in search snippets. It is about the present anyway.

**Worth knowing**
- Search results said Huang has resigned as Nvidia's chief executive (CNN, Wikipedia's "1993–2026", a CBS headline). I saw this only in snippets and did not check it.
- Some 2026 pages describe events I can't confirm, such as GPT-6 Astra. Please check each source page yourself.

I used 10 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
